sections.text:
ex collectaneis hausta esse videntur Περὶ τεράτων καὶ σημείων, quibus Artemido-
rus (III, 28) vel potius auctor eius Apollonius Attalensis usus est (Susemihl, Griech.
Lit. Alexandr., I, 873). Ideo autem maxime dignum est quod edatur excerptum
Mutinense quod ex eodem fonte fluxit atque capitula 17-20 LYDI de Ostentis, ad
Capitonem referenda, si Curtio Wachsmuth assentiamur. At illis eandem esse
originem atque huic fragmento primo obtutu manifestum fiet, si e. g. versus de
Capricorno, quibus incipit scriptor byzantinus, contuleris. Itaque haud minimi est
momenti hoc Melampodis frustulum et ad auctores Iohannis Lydi cognoscendos
et ad lacunas codicis Caseolini explendas.
F. C.]
sections.en:
they seem to have been drawn from the collections Περὶ τεράτων καὶ σημείων ('On portents and signs'), which Artemido-
rus (III, 28) or rather his source Apollonius of Attalia used (Susemihl, Griech.
Lit. Alexandr., I, 873). But for this reason the excerpt from Modena is especially worthy of being published,
because it flowed from the same source as chapters 17-20 of LYDUS On Ostents, to be referred to
Capito, if we agree with Curtius Wachsmuth. But that they have the same
origin as this fragment will become manifest at first glance, if for example you compare the lines about
Capricorn, with which the Byzantine writer begins. Therefore this little fragment of Melampus is of no small
importance both for knowing the sources of John Lydus
and for filling the lacunae of the Caseoline codex.
[F. C.]

summary.headline: Lunar Omens in Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer
summary.text: Astrological omens for the Moon and Sun in Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer: eclipses, blood-red moons, thunder, fog, earthquakes, winds, and other phenomena portend war, famine, destruction, crop abundance or scarcity, and upheaval. A critical note links the Melampus fragment to Artemidorus, Apollonius of Attalia, John Lydus’s On Ostents, Capito, and the Caseoline codex.
